_comment: Service conditions a requirement may depend on (#638, #677). Read by
app/service_scope.py. A requirement is SPECIFIC to a condition when its
standard is one of `standards` (read by standard_ids, so any spelling and
the equivalent names match) or its own text carries one of
`requirement_markers`. It does NOT APPLY only when the submittal's own
datasheet DECLARES the condition absent: a field whose label carries one
of `field_labels` and whose value reads as `declared_absent`. Declared
present, or not declared at all, keeps the requirement a check - unknown
is never 'does not apply'. Edit this file to add a condition; no code

#725 F6: a condition with "mode": "value" is declared by WHAT the application fields say: present when a stated field in `field_labels` names one of `satisfied_by`; absent only when such fields are stated and none does (the stated value is cited). Its markers are also read from the clause heading and its parents. Nothing stated keeps it a check.

#754 F5b: `required_standards` names the standards a datasheet that DECLARES the condition present must be reviewed against (sour service stated: NACE MR0175 / ISO 15156, one standard under two names). applicability.standards_check adds them to the required set; one the contractor did not cite gets one CRS comment. A cited `standards` entry on a datasheet that declares the condition ABSENT gets a "does not appear to apply" note. Generic: no per-document rules.
